description: MAIN-PARA's WHEN OTHER invalid-key arm, derived from app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:138-141 and the paragraphs it reaches at :289-301 and :319-338 - transaction CB00 re-entered with the CLEAR key, which is the REENTER half of gate G38 and the fourth and last arm of the AID dispatch. It is this directory's primary gate G30 proof and its only consumer of a CSMSG01Y literal. IN SOURCE ORDER. :101-102 set ERR-FLG-OFF and USR-MODIFIED-NO, :104-105 move SPACES to WS-MESSAGE and to ERRMSGO OF COBIL0AO, :107 finds EIBCALEN non-zero so the cold-start arm is not taken, :111 copies the travelled area over CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, :112 finds CDEMO-PGM-REENTER true because CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives 1 - so the whole first-entry block at :113-122 is skipped, which is why MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COBIL0AO at :114 does NOT run here and the three data fields end as the bytes the RECEIVE delivered rather than as nulls - and :124 performs RECEIVE-BILLPAY-SCREEN. THE ORDERED DISPATCH, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS CASE. The EVALUATE EIBAID at :125-142 has four arms and exactly one order: WHEN DFHENTER at :126, WHEN DFHPF3 at :128, WHEN DFHPF4 at :136, and WHEN OTHER at :138 LAST. COBOL EVALUATE is ordered - the first matching WHEN wins and WHEN OTHER is the default - so the arm this case pins is reached ONLY because all three named arms were tested first and all three failed, and that conjunction is precisely what gate G30 requires this case to prove. An implementation that reordered the arms, that promoted WHEN OTHER above a named one, or that let a matched arm fall through into the next would be a different program (AAP rule R7), and none of those defects is visible from a case that only ever presses ENTER. THE KEY IS THE CLEAR KEY, AND THE CHOICE IS ARGUED RATHER THAN ARBITRARY. The AID is DFHCLEAR, the EBCDIC underscore X'6D', taken from common.CicsAid because DFHAID is IBM-supplied and absent from this repository (risk R-D). Four reasons for it over a mid-range PF key. It is provably outside {DFHENTER, DFHPF3, DFHPF4}: a search of all 572 lines of COBIL00C.cbl for DFH finds those three mnemonics at :126, :128 and :136 and no fourth, the remaining matches being COPY DFHAID at :84, COPY DFHBMSCA at :85, the DFHCOMMAREA at :91 and :111, DFHGREEN at :526 and the DFHRESP macros of the file paragraphs. It is not a PF key at all, so the arm is shown to catch a whole other class of AID rather than merely a PF number outside a handled range. The only occurrence of DFHCLEAR anywhere in the COBOL is app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy:24, which maps it to that copybook's CLEAR token - and COBIL00C copies neither CSSTRPFY nor CSSETATY, so nothing folds CLEAR into a handled case here and the key lands on WHEN OTHER by this program's own inline three-way test. And it is what an operator would actually press: app/bms/COBIL00.bms:135 carries the trailing legend 'ENTER=Continue  F3=Back  F4=Clear', so this screen binds clearing to F4 and the physical CLEAR key is an error rather than a shortcut. WHAT THE ARM DOES, IN ITS THREE STATEMENTS. :139 MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG raises the error flag, which is program state and not a return code. :140 MOVE CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY TO WS-MESSAGE. :141 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN - exactly ONE emission, which is why sends carries one entry and why an implementation that sent twice would fail here. No MOVE -1 TO xxxL appears on this arm, so no cursor is requested and cursorField is absent rather than blank: the terminal applies the mapset's own IC field, which app/bms/COBIL00.bms:85 puts on ACTIDIN. That is a real difference from case06, whose DFHPF4 arm reaches INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :562 and does declare ACTIDINL. THE BYTE-EXACT MESSAGE AND ITS TWO TRUNCATIONS. app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy:20-21 declares CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY PIC X(50); the literal inside the quotes measures 49 characters - 40 of text, 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...' counted mechanically including the three-dot ellipsis, followed by 9 physical spaces - and COBOL supplies one more space to fill the picture, so the field holds 40 + 10 = 50. :140 then moves it into WS-MESSAGE, which COBIL00C.cbl:39 declares PIC X(80): an alphanumeric move is left-justified and PADS ON THE RIGHT, so WS-MESSAGE holds 40 characters of text and 40 spaces. :293 moves WS-MESSAGE into ERRMSGO, which app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY:140 declares PIC X(78): the same rule in the other direction, so the move TRUNCATES ON THE RIGHT and the two bytes discarded are spaces. The surviving field is 40 characters of text and 38 spaces, exactly 78 - and 78 is what this case asserts, untrimmed, because the differ compares fixed-width fields and a trimmed 40-character expectation is a width mismatch rather than a tidier way of saying the same thing. Both moves act on the right, per AAP 0.3.7. WHY THERE IS ONE EMITTED MESSAGE AND WHICH CHANNEL IT IS ON. expectedMessages carries a single entry on the WS_MESSAGE_80 channel, holding the 80-byte intermediate: 40 characters of text and 40 spaces. That width exists nowhere else in the fixture - the send can only show the 78 bytes that reached the screen - so asserting it is the only way to pin the middle link of the X(50) to X(80) to X(78) chain and prove the pad happened before the truncation rather than instead of it. It is deliberately not DISPLAY_LINE: all six DISPLAY statements in the program, at :366, :397, :430, :461, :490 and :541, sit in the WHEN OTHER arm of a file operation inside PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, and none is reachable from here, so claiming one would claim an emission the program never made. And it is not SCREEN_ERRMSG_78, because those 78 bytes are asserted where screen text belongs - as ERRMSGO on the send that produced it - and asserting them twice would double-count one fact. WHAT SURVIVES THE ARM, WHICH IS THE SECOND ASSERTION THIS CASE MAKES. Because the AID never matched DFHENTER, PROCESS-ENTER-KEY at :154-244 never runs, and because it never matched DFHPF4, CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN at :552-555 and INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :560-566 never run either. ACTIDINI, CURBALI and CONFIRMI therefore keep exactly what the RECEIVE delivered, and the case seeds all three so that the survival is an assertion rather than a tautology: ACTIDINI carries account 00000000001 and CURBALI carries +0000000194.00, which are row 1 of app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt - ACCT-ID 00000000001 and ACCT-CURR-BAL 00000001940{, whose trailing { is the zoned overpunch for a positive digit zero, so the value is 194.00 rendered through the PIC +9999999999.99 mask of :193 with its forced sign and zero-filled digits - and CONFIRMI carries 'Y'. That 'Y' is the sharpest part of the case: a confirmation was typed and the account was on the screen, and still nothing was read, written, rewritten or computed, because the key was not ENTER. ACTIDINO, CURBALO and CONFIRMO are asserted at those same values, NOT blanked - the exact opposite of case06, which is what makes the two cases distinguishable at all. All three are addressed as xxxO items on the send because app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY:79 declares COBIL0AO REDEFINES COBIL0AI, so the input and output views share one span and :298 sends FROM(COBIL0AO). CURBALI is seeded even though ACTIDIN and CONFIRM are the only UNPROT fields on the mapset: app/bms/COBIL00.bms:103 declares CURBAL ATTRB=(ASKIP,FSET,NORM), and FSET sets the modified-data tag, so a 3270 returns the field even though the operator cannot type into it. The six header items are not seeded, because POPULATE-HEADER-INFO overwrites every one of them at :323-338 before the send regardless of what arrived. THE CONTEXT STAYS 1. No XCTL occurs on this arm, so RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN is never performed and its MOVE ZEROS TO CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT at :280 is not reached: the context leaves as the 1 it arrived as and the next invocation takes the re-entry arm again. Control falls out of the EVALUATE to the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) at :146-149, which is why the termination is RETURN_TRANSID and why the mapset and map of :296-297 are named rather than a next program. WHAT DOES NOT HAPPEN. No dataset is touched, because READ-ACCTDAT-FILE, UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE, READ-CXACAIX-FILE, the three TRANSACT browse paragraphs and WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE are reached only from PROCESS-ENTER-KEY: inputs is empty and expectedWrites, expectedFinalState and expectedDatasets are empty BY DERIVATION rather than by omission, an empty expectedWrites being the positive assertion that nothing was written. normalisations is empty because no fixture is seeded, so the cardxref 36-to-50 pad has nothing to apply to. The RECEIVE at :308-314 names RESP(WS-RESP-CD) and RESP2(WS-REAS-CD) and the program tests neither on any path, unlike the six paragraphs that do open an EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD - READ-ACCTDAT-FILE at :356, UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE at :387, READ-CXACAIX-FILE at :420, STARTBR-TRANSACT-FILE at :451, READPREV-TRANSACT-FILE at :484 and WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE at :522, with ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE at :501 the one file paragraph that also checks nothing; that absence is preserved rather than tidied into a check the source does not perform. The attribute map is empty and must stay empty: COBIL00C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY - its COPY list at :63-85 is COCOM01Y, COBIL00, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CVACT01Y, CVACT03Y, CVTRA05Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - and DFHRED appears nowhere in its 572 lines, so there is no red-and-asterisk highlight to expect on this or any other path. The red the operator sees is the mapset's own: app/bms/COBIL00.bms:127-130 declares ERRMSG ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) COLOR=RED LENGTH=78. The program's single attribute write is MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC OF COBIL0AO at :526, on the successful transaction-WRITE arm this path never reaches. THERE IS NO MONETARY ARITHMETIC ON THIS PATH, and saying so is better than leaving it as a silent absence: the program's one COMPUTE, ACCT-CURR-BAL = ACCT-CURR-BAL - TRAN-AMT at :234, is inside PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, and so is the MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO WS-CURR-BAL at :193 that would recompute the edited balance. CURBALO here is echoed bytes, not a computed number, so no BigDecimal, no scale and no rounding mode is asserted - the truncating arithmetic of COBIL00C, which carries no ROUNDED phrase because the keyword appears zero times in all 28 programs, is the business of the cases that reach :211-235. THE RETURN CODE IS 0 AND THAT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT THE SOURCE. COBIL00C assigns RETURN-CODE nowhere and contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD', so no path in it can end with a non-zero step status; the error on this arm is signalled by WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y' at :139 and by the message on the screen, and nothing else. STATELESSNESS. EIBCALEN is 218 - the 160 bytes app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy declares for CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, being 34 for CDEMO-GENERAL-INFO, 84 for CDEMO-CUSTOMER-INFO, 12 for CDEMO-ACCOUNT-INFO, 16 for CDEMO-CARD-INFO and 14 for CDEMO-MORE-INFO, plus the 58 bytes of the CDEMO-CB00-INFO group COBIL00C.cbl:64-72 appends in place. The one commarea item this arm reads is CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT, tested at :112, so it is the only one the request declares; the response pins all sixteen shared carriers at their declared widths, none of which this arm writes, so they travel back exactly as they arrived. All of it - the area, the AID and the screen values - travels in the payload, so no server-side session state exists or is implied (gate G37, AAP rule R6). UNIT KIND, AND WHY IT IS THE CONTROLLER SEAM. The subject is the dispatch at :125-142, and an AID is expressible only through screenRequest.aid, so only a CONTROLLER_POJO case can state it: BillPaymentService has no AID-bearing entry point - its seams are processEnterKey(BillPaymentRequest), processEnterKey(actIdIn, confirm, commarea) and the effect-only invalidKeyPressed(PaymentState) - so a service-kind declaration could not select an arm on EIBAID at all, and the header projection, the mapset and map names and the echoed commarea are the controller's output besides. CONTROLLER_POJO means the handler constructed and called as a plain Java object: no HTTP, no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container, no JobLauncher and no application context anywhere in the path, which is exactly what gate G51 asks for. The three effects the arm performs are still the service's, in BillPaymentService.invalidKeyPressed(PaymentState), which raises the flag, moves SystemMessages.CCDA_MSG_INVALID_KEY into the 80-byte message and performs the send; what the controller owns is the ordered dispatch that reaches it and the ten-field projection that is observed. PROVENANCE. Every value above is STATICALLY DERIVED - read out of the COBOL paragraph that produces it and cross-checked against the xxxI and xxxO PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY, the DFHMDF definitions and 24-by-80 DFHMDI of app/bms/COBIL00.bms, the PIC X(50) literal of app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy, the two PIC X(40) VALUE literals of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, the eight-byte MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS groups of app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, the 160-byte layout of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy and row 1 of app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt - and it was NOT CAPTURED FROM A LIVE COBOL EXECUTION, not one byte of it, because such a capture is empirically impossible in this environment: no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, no Language Environment CEE services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR absent from the repository - which is why the DFHCLEAR mnemonic this case declares comes from common.CicsAid, the single reproduction of DFHAID, rather than from a copybook (AAP 0.7.6 documents eight verified blockers, 0.9.11 records the substitution as risk R-A escalated for confirmation rather than absorbed, and 0.9.12 records the missing copybooks as risk R-D). DETERMINISM. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32, the instant the program's own version footer at :571 carries, so CURDATEO is 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO is 23:12:32 rather than whatever the wall clock said - the header is read once per send from an injected Clock through common.DateHeader and never from a captured now, and every case in this directory pins that same instant. Two-digit month, day and hour, no midnight and no daylight-saving edge, so neither rendering is ambiguous. US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default, which for a nine-fixture ASCII corpus and a twelve-dataset EBCDIC one is the difference between a comparison and a coincidence. THE EIGHTY-BYTE WS-MESSAGE IS NOT DECLARED AS AN EMITTED MESSAGE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: an online program emits nothing. app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:299 moves WS-MESSAGE into ERRMSGO and the value leaves through EXEC CICS SEND MAP, so the observable form is the send - pinned field for field in expectedResponse at the seventy-eight-byte width app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY declares, which is also the width at which the two-byte tail of an over-long message is lost.
